text: On which Leeds country estate is Emmerdale's purpose-built village set?
info: Harewood House, between Leeds and Harrogate; the set has been there since 1997.

text: Which island in Poole Harbour hosted Baden-Powell's first Scout camp, in 1907?
info: Brownsea Island, in Poole Harbour, Dorset; also a red squirrel stronghold.

text: Which Bristol Channel island once issued its own 'puffin' coins and still has its own stamps?
info: Lundy, about 12 miles off the north Devon coast.

text: Which steep Yorkshire fishing village south of Whitby was a famous smugglers' haunt?
info: Robin Hood's Bay, on the North Yorkshire coast; also the end of the Coast to Coast walk.

text: Which Victorian resort near Redcar has Britain's oldest working water-powered cliff lift?
info: Saltburn-by-the-Sea; the cliff lift opened in 1884.

text: Which Northumberland fishing village is famous for its oak-smoked kippers?
info: Craster, on the coast below Dunstanburgh Castle.

text: From which Northumberland harbour do the boats leave for the Farne Islands?
info: Seahouses, a few miles south of Bamburgh.

text: Which little bay between Tynemouth and Whitley Bay drew Victorian painters, including the American Winslow Homer?
info: Cullercoats, on the North Tyneside coast; Homer stayed in 1881 and 1882.
